sections.heading: The doors are open
items: DragonBreak Online's alpha is open to everyone in our Discord, and it is free to play.
There will be no wipe from here on. What you earn, build and forge from tonight is yours to keep.
For now the alpha is Bruma and the lands around it, high in the Jerall Mountains. More of Tamriel opens as the alpha grows.

sections.heading: A fresh start for everyone
items: To open the alpha on even ground, every character was reset once. Skills, character levels, learned spells and schools of magic are back to the start.
Items and gold went too, and you begin with a miner's clothes and boots, a pickaxe, a woodcutter's axe and 50 gold. Every chest and container in the world was emptied.
Every house is free again for the holds' officials to grant, and whoever holds one may open a business in it anew. Guild membership starts over, and your faith is yours to choose again.
Vampirism and lycanthropy are gone: everyone begins mortal, looking as they did before the curse, and the Blood Crown lies unclaimed.
Your characters, their names, their looks and your character slots are all still yours.

sections.heading: Thank you, playtesters
items: Everyone who helped test DragonBreak Online before the alpha now has a second character slot. Your double skill progress has its own note.

sections.heading: Help and guides
items: Something wrong in game? Type /bug followed by what happened, while it's in front of you.
If the game closes or won't start, open the launcher's gear, then Troubleshooting > Report a Problem, or open a ticket on our Discord.
The guides to skills, magic, crafting, races, religion, the holds and the rules are at dragonbreakonline.com/guides.

sections.heading: Double skill progress for 24 hours
items: Everyone who helped test DragonBreak Online before the alpha gets double skill progress for 24 hours. It starts at your first login after the alpha opens on 1 October at 05:00 UTC, whichever character you play.
The 24 hours run in real time, online or not, and cover every character on your account. Type /boost to see how long you have left.
Your work still counts towards the usual hourly and daily limits; each bit of it simply moves your skill twice as far.
Log in by 8 October at 05:00 UTC to claim it.

sections.heading: Skills
items: The playtester double-progress boost has ended early while we rebalance how fast skills grow.

sections.heading: Items
items: Items that only appeared to be in your pack after a dropped or harvested item are now corrected straight away.

sections.heading: Vampire Lords
items: Revert Form on the Shout key now turns a Vampire Lord back into their own shape. You can also type /beast to turn back at any time.

sections.heading: Vampires
items: Vampires: feeding no longer leaves your vampire spells missing after you log back in. Anyone affected gets them back automatically.

sections.heading: Lag no longer fails you
items: Praying: a prayer you held through to the end is no longer refused because your connection was slow.
Mining and woodcutting: a slow connection no longer loses a round you played. It counts even if it reaches the server minutes late.
Skinning: standing still while you skin no longer fails the cut.
Reading: a right answer now counts even if it reaches the server up to 30 seconds after the candle goes out, instead of 2.5 seconds.
Struggling against bonds: a slow connection no longer loses your pulls.

sections.heading: Lockpicking
items: The lock no longer freezes after two misses in a row, or after a try on a tumbler that is not the loose one.
Leaving a lock with Escape no longer leaves every chest and door unresponsive for a minute.

sections.heading: Rites
items: The strike window in a rite is wider and more forgiving of lag.

Until the next game update, Molag Bal's Embrace and the Great Hunt cannot be begun. A rite that can kill must not be lost to a slow connection, and the update lets your own game judge each strike. They open again with it.
Until then, losing a Blood Fever rite or Hircine's Hunt breaks the fever without killing you.

title: Three spell tomes in their proper schools

sections.heading: Magic
items: Spectral Arrow, Command Daedra and Paralyze are now ranked in their proper schools: Conjuration Apprentice, Conjuration Expert and Alteration Expert.

sections.heading: Werewolves and Vampire Lords
items: Dying in beast form: the "You're down!" panel now takes the mouse, so you can choose Give up.

sections.heading: Blessings
items: Most blessings that come as a spell are now cast on you when they are granted. Until now they only put a 'Blessing of' spell in your spellbook and did nothing.
Your blessing is cast on you again when you log back in, and again when the spell's own time (eight hours, twelve for Auri-El) runs out before your blessing does.
If you were blessed before this update, the useless spell leaves your spellbook and the blessing is cast on you instead.

sections.heading: Offerings
items: Standing up from a prayer before you begin it no longer makes the shrine rest, so you can touch a shrine, make your /offer and pray straight away.

title: A crash no longer costs you the temple

sections.heading: Falling in battle
items: A crash no longer costs you a fall: once the launcher reports the crash, your body cannot be harmed for up to ten minutes, and a fall that came after the crash wakes you where you fell, at full health, without Death's Chill. Quitting the game still counts as a fall.

sections.heading: A charter of your own
items: You can now found a faction of your own, a company or a cult. Type /charter found and a name to start its charter, or /charter cult and a name for a cult.

A charter needs three players on three different accounts: you as its Founder, who will lead it, an Officer and a Sergeant. Invite them with /charter invite and their name; they agree with /charter confirm and the charter's number.
Up to two more founding members can join it in any other role: Officer, Sergeant, Mage, Blacksmith, Tailor or Member.
Give it a purpose with /charter pitch. If you like, give it a seat: stand at a house you or another founding member owns and type /charter seat here.

Then /charter submit sends it to the GMs. Once they approve it, your faction is on the Faction page of your journal (F3), with the seven ranks from Leader to Member and a treasury of its own. There is no fee.

sections.heading: The rules
items: A faction's name must fit the world: not an existing faction, hold or region, and not one of the Elder Scrolls' own factions that are not in the game yet. Only a cult may be named for a Daedric Prince.
You have 48 hours to gather your founders and submit, and an account can be on one charter at a time. If the GMs decline a charter, its founder can file a new one after a week.
A faction's leader can ask the GMs to disband it with /charter disband and a reason. If they agree, its treasury goes to the player who founded it.
/charter on its own shows your charter and what to do next.

title: Iron Falchion out of loot for now

sections.heading: Loot
items: The Iron Falchion's model comes without its texture in Beyond Skyrim itself, so it no longer drops until we fix the model. If you already have one, it stays yours.
Camp chests now hold only weapons of their own land: a camp in Bruma gives Cyrodiil's weapons, not Skyrim's.

sections.heading: Dungeons
items: Weapons and armour from chests and enemies now match the difficulty you claim a dungeon on: iron and leather at Novice, steel and elven at Adept, steel plate and some glass at Expert, the most glass at Master.
Boss chests and masters give better pieces than the rest of the dungeon, and a harder lock guards better gear.
Ebony, Daedric, Dragon, Stalhrim and Orcish gear never drops.

sections.heading: Naming your character
items: A name may now end in a regnal number from II to X, like Titus Mede II, and the name of a character you deleted is free again at once.

sections.heading: Wildlife
items: Bruma's boars bite much less hard. A new character can now take seven bites before going down, where three were enough before.
They also go down faster: a new character with an iron sword now fells one in about six blows, where it took nearly thirty.
A creature's hit that is scaled down, such as a boar's power bite or a blow your Defense armour softens, no longer knocks you down when the smaller hit would not have.

sections.heading: Temples
items: Priests can now study Restoration at the temples' study points, the way mages use Study Magic. In Bruma, that is the Cathedral of St Martin.
The new lecterns in the temples have a Preach prompt. Sermons are coming soon, and for now that is what it tells you.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Walking into a cave mouth that you cannot enter yet (it rests for you, or another party holds it) no longer freezes you in front of it. You are set down just outside instead.

sections.heading: Update
items: Update through the launcher: there's a new plugin.

title: The Bank of Bruma Belongs to Bruma

sections.heading: Around Bruma and the land
items: The Bank of Bruma now counts as part of Bruma inside as well as out, and its doors are named: Bank of Bruma on the way in, Bruma on the way out.
Door names across the land now read properly, for example the Cathedral of St Martin in Bruma.
Camp chests are for players: their guards no longer pocket the loot.
Fort Caractacus is no longer a dungeon to claim and clear. It is the Legion's fort, and its doors open like any other.
Ebony, Daedric, Dragon, Stalhrim and Orcish gear no longer turns up in dungeon or camp loot.

sections.heading: Bruma pays its due to the Empire
items: Bruma is a county of the Empire, and from the next weekly reckoning (Sunday 00:00 UTC) the Empire takes its tithe: a tenth of the property tax collected on Cyrodiil land goes into the Imperial Legion's treasury.
The tithe is reckoned on the property tax taken that week, not on the treasury's savings, so it begins once a county's Count sets a tax. A county that taxes nothing owes no tithe.

If the Count is online at the Sunday reckoning (00:00 UTC), the reckoning message tells them what the tithe came to. Anything the treasury could not pay is owed, and taken first the next week. The Legion's own forts pay none, and Skyrim's Holds, independent since the Legion withdrew, pay nothing.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: A prayer to Mehrunes Dagon no longer breaks the fever that turns you into a vampire or a werewolf. A prayer to any other Daedric Prince never did.
The calendar now reads 4E 211 when you type /time. The Wait menu and your journal follow with the next client update.
When staff rename a character, the old name is free again, and the new name is kept for that character alone.
Rent held for an inn's owner while they are away now goes to that owner, even if the inn has changed hands since.
Only Lead GMs and above can raise or clear warbands and raids, from the Place tool as well as from chat.
Masks can't be duplicated by pressing the mask key rapidly.
Signatures can't use staff titles (such as Admin, Moderator or Game Master) or blocked words.

title: Werewolves Seen in Human Shape, For Now

sections.heading: Beast forms
items: For now, other players see a werewolf in its human shape, as they already do a Vampire Lord. A werewolf's howl could crash the game of anyone watching; the next client update fixes that, and the beasts come back once it has been tested.
Your own werewolf form looks and plays as before on your screen.

title: Steadier Beasts, and Characters That Act

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Fixed a likely cause of crashes near a werewolf howling or a Vampire Lord casting. For now, other players won't see a Vampire Lord's spell effects; the spells still hit as normal.
Your own character's name no longer changes on your screen when someone nearby puts on or takes off a mask.
Auto-run now switches off when a skinning, mining or chopping round takes the keyboard.

sections.heading: Animations
items: Characters act out everyday things: studying a notice board, and saluting when introducing themselves.
Potions and draughts no longer play a drinking animation; they still work instantly.

sections.heading: Your school
items: Mages now follow a school of magic: Destruction, Illusion, Conjuration or Alteration. Choose your first school on the Arcane Arts page of the Skills menu (K), or at a Study Magic spot. The same page shows all four school meters.
A school's meter rises as you cast its spells, and you can read a tome of that school only up to your rank in it. When Arcane Arts reaches 76 you may take up a second school.
Every spell you already know stays yours, whatever school you choose.

sections.heading: Study and classes
items: Study Magic at the Synod Conclave's bookcases and at the Study Magic spots: up to 20 minutes of study in any 4 hours, until you learn your first spell through Arcane Arts.

Class Lecterns stand in the Synod Conclave, Frostcrag Spire and the College of Winterhold's Hall of the Elements. A teacher of the Synod or the College can hold a class there, and every student in the room learns from it.

sections.heading: Alteration
items: Alteration belongs to priests and mages both. A priest takes it up through Priest; a mage who chose Alteration, through Arcane Arts.

sections.heading: Alchemist and Harvesting
items: Picking plants, mushrooms and fruit no longer trains Alchemist; it trains Harvesting only, as it always should have. Eating ingredients no longer trains Alchemist either.
Alchemist grows from working at the alchemy lab.

sections.heading: Sea Salt Deposits
items: Sea Salt Deposits now glow for Miners while they have salt to give, and go dark while the seam rests, so they are much easier to spot in the snow. Thanks to GroundedPasta for the report.

title: Dragon Bone and Scales Come From Dragons

sections.heading: Materials
items: Dragon bone and dragon scales now come only from slain dragons. Dragon gear breaks down into its other materials.

sections.heading: Cooking
items: Every dish can now be cooked in every land. Cooked Boar Meat and other dishes from Solstheim and Morrowind were refused in Bruma as foreign designs; they no longer are. What you can cook still depends on the ingredients you carry.
Gear, cloaks and metal ingots keep their homelands as before.

sections.heading: Werewolves
items: A werewolf who belongs to no pack is now a Lone Wolf. The Werewolf tab in your Skills menu (K), /hunt and /status say so, and a pack member sees their pack and rank there instead.
It is a name for now: nothing about your beast changes with it. A pack still takes you in only by invitation.

sections.heading: A vampire's first meal
items: A newly turned vampire's powers sleep until their first feed. Go more than six hours (game time) without blood and your body starts to wither: wounds and stamina recover more slowly each hour until you drink. Blood lifts it at once.
Ordinary food barely eases a vampire's hunger.

sections.heading: Feeding
items: Feeding now takes a few seconds, and you kneel over the body as you drink. The higher your blood rank, the quicker you feed. Moving away or being struck breaks the feed.
From Nightstalker you can Feed Deeply on a captive: it takes longer, heals you faster for a while and keeps the thirst away longer, and your victim blacks out.
Vampires can now ask anyone for their blood. The other player sees a prompt and can offer their neck or resist.
Feeding can leave blood around a young or hungry vampire's mouth. It stays until you wash it off in water.
Werewolves in beast form now play their feeding animation, and a feed takes a few seconds.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: When your thirst grows, Vampiric Drain in your hand now becomes the stronger drain instead of vanishing from your hand.

title: Pray or Perform the Rite at the Shrine

sections.heading: Shrines
items: Touching a shrine of Molag Bal, Hircine, Arkay or Stendarr now opens a panel: Pray, or Perform the Rite. When you can't do one of them, the panel tells you why.
Choosing a rite shows what it can cost before anything happens. Only the rite's own button (Kneel, Run the Hunt or Offer the soul gem) begins it, and Cancel takes you back. /rite still works.

title: Your Curse in the Skills Menu

sections.heading: Werewolves and vampires
items: Werewolves and vampires now have their own tab in the Skills menu (K): your rank and what the next one brings, your thirst or your beast, your first meal, and your powers.
The werewolf's howl that senses the living is now named for the Totem of the Hunt, as in Skyrim. Howl of the Pack is the howl that calls wolves.

sections.heading: Dungeons
items: Rooms that stood empty in a claimed dungeon now hold enemies of that dungeon's own kind, among them the back caves of Fingerbowl Cave and Serpent's Trail near Bruma. Where a room's own inhabitants had simply never appeared, like the goblins of Frostiron Mine, they are back where they belong.

title: The Goblins of Dusk Thorn Stand Together

sections.heading: Dusk Thorn Camp
items: The goblins of Dusk Thorn Camp no longer fight each other: they are one tribe now, and they turn on you together. Thanks to Onny for testing the camp.

sections.heading: Boars
items: The boars around Bruma no longer turn their tusks on each other: a herd sticks together now, and charges you as one. Thanks to GroundedPasta for the report.

sections.heading: Smithing and enchanting
items: How far you can temper now follows your Blacksmith rank: Fine as a Novice, Superior as an Apprentice, Exquisite as a Journeyman, Epic as an Expert, and Legendary as a Master.
How strong your enchantments can be now follows your Enchanter rank, from half the strength of the best enchantments found in the world as a Novice to twice it as a Master.
Items you have already tempered or enchanted keep what they have.

title: Dusk Thorn Camp and the Boars of Bruma

sections.heading: The wilds
items: Goblins have made camp east of Bruma: Dusk Thorn Camp. Eight goblins guard it, and their chest gives each adventurer a share once an hour. It glows while it has something for you.
Wild boars now roam the hills east of Bruma. They give boar meat and a tusk.
Eleven new Sea Salt Deposits line the rivers east of Bruma for Miners.

title: Crafting Follows the Land and Its People

sections.heading: Crafting
items: Gear is now made where it belongs. A smith in Cyrodiil can forge Cyrodilic, Imperial, Elven, Daedric, Ebony and Glass work, but not the arms of Skyrim, Morrowind or Solstheim; a refused craft keeps your materials.
A people can always make their own: an Orc forges Orcish anywhere, a Nord Nordic and Skaal work, a Dunmer chitin and bonemold, and so on for every race with a craft of its own.

title: Client 0.3.70: Contracts on the Expedition Board

sections.heading: Contracts
items: The expedition board now has a Contracts tab: read the hunting notices your area has posted, take one, see your progress and give it up, all from the board. /contract still works.

sections.heading: Getting it
items: The launcher downloads this update the next time you press Play.

title: Better Loot, Brewing Help and Saltier Deposits

sections.heading: Dungeons
items: Ordinary dungeons give their full loot again; expeditions keep their leaner chests.
A fallen warrior can now hand over the weapon or armour they were using when you search their body.
Chests that hold loot glow, and go dark once you have emptied them, not as soon as you open them.

sections.heading: Alchemy and gathering
items: Using an alchemy lab now also shows every potion the ingredients you carry can make, and which two to combine.
A Sea Salt Deposit gives 4 salt a round instead of 2.

sections.heading: Champions
items: Now and then a wild beast or a dungeon's creature rises as a champion: named, bigger and far tougher than its kind.
Everyone who fought it shares one reward by the damage they dealt: a purse of gold and a chance of a gem, with a bonus for fighting together. A champion also counts twice toward a hunting contract.

title: Only the Animal Comes Off an Animal

sections.heading: Hunting
items: A hunted animal now gives only what comes from the animal: meat, hides, pelts, antlers, tusks, horns, claws and the like. Deer no longer carry silver rings, and bears no longer carry gems or gold. Giants still carry their gear.

Every animal now gives meat: wolves and foxes give dog meat, bears, sabre cats and mountain lions give beef, skeevers give rat meat and slaughterfish give their own fish. Boars give boar meat and a tusk.

sections.heading: Chests
items: A giant camp chest now glows while it has something for you and goes dark once you have picked through it, until it refills an hour later. Dungeon chests already glow for the party that claimed the dungeon. A chest or barrel that does not glow has nothing in it.

title: Dressed After Death, and the Blood Crown

sections.heading: Fixes
items: If you die while logged out, you no longer come back naked: your outfit is put back on when you log in, and after every return from the temple.
A vampire now only holds the spells of their own stage; spells from an earlier stage no longer appear and then vanish when you equip them.

sections.heading: Vampires
items: A new pure-blood is now told when the Blood Crown is held by another vampire: slay its holder to take the Vampire Lord's form. /blood tells a pure-blood where the Crown stands.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Every dropdown list in our windows now opens properly: the realm panel's choices (capital, tribute, wars, raids and treaties), faction ranks and the staff tools. Before, their lists opened where you could not see them.

sections.heading: Getting it
items: The launcher downloads this update the next time you press Play.

sections.heading: Hunting
items: Pressing E on a dead deer or other wild animal now hands you its meat, antlers and anything else it carried, after you skin it or when it has no hide. Before, the loot window could show nothing even though the meat was there.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: A mining seam or chopping block now belongs to the one person working it until their round ends; a second worker waits their turn.
Plants, torches, coin purses and wisp stalks stay picked after a server restart.
A lost starter tool is replaced at most once a day.

sections.heading: Smithing and armor
items: Dragonscale armor now protects better than Ebony, piece for piece, and Dragonplate already did. Your inventory shows the new numbers. Daedric stays the strongest.
The Blacksmith's ranks list Dragonbone and Dragonscale at Master, beside Daedric, above Ebony at Expert.
Silver weapons join the Blacksmith's ranks at Apprentice, beside Steel.

sections.heading: Loot
items: Artifacts are no longer found as loot. Legendary arms and armour, Daedric artifacts and Dragon Priest masks come to the champions of the realm through the story, awarded by the staff.
Ebony and Daedric gear no longer turns up in any dungeon chest or on any body, as intended; a few containers could still hand it out.

sections.heading: Combat
items: After you are staggered or shoved, you cannot be staggered or shoved again for 3 seconds, so two attackers can no longer keep you reeling.

sections.heading: Champions
items: A champion now pays one reward per kill, shared between the fighters by the damage each dealt, with one gem roll. A group earns a bonus on top, up to twice a solo kill.

sections.heading: Mining, woodcutting and reading
items: A mined seam rests for 45 minutes and a chopping block for 10 after someone works it, for everyone.
Walking away from a mining, chopping or reading round now counts like a failed one, with the same short wait.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Pressing X on a player who has logged out now says they are gone, instead of asking you to get closer.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: A window of ours that opened while a game menu was up (character creation, your inventory, a container) took the keyboard away from that menu until you alt-tabbed. It now waits until the game menu closes and then takes the keyboard.
When the game stops hearing your keyboard, it now takes it back by itself, so you no longer need to alt-tab out and back in.

sections.heading: Getting it
items: The launcher downloads this update the next time you press Play.

title: Hunting, Dungeons, Combat and Fair Play

sections.heading: Hunting
items: A skinned deer now opens like any other body, so its venison, antlers and coin can be taken. The same goes for a hide beyond your Skinner rank: you are told who could take the hide, and the body opens for the rest.
A contract kill counts only inside the notice's own hold, as the notice says.

sections.heading: Dungeons
items: Only the party that claimed a dungeon can open its chests and loot its dead.
A dungeon's rest now follows you across characters, and a party can only claim a dungeon once every member's rest has run out. The refusal says who is still resting.

sections.heading: Combat
items: A spell can no longer hit the same target again faster than it can be cast.
A Vampire Lord's bat form now has a 12-second wait, the untouchable state ends when the form does, and nobody can strike while untouchable.
Beast claws are no longer treated as Martial Arts fists, and someone carried or held fast by paralysis can no longer land blows.
A party member's hit right after a server restart is now softened like any other friendly fire.

sections.heading: Rest and reading
items: You can no longer go to sleep in a bed within five minutes of a fight, or while struggling or being robbed.
Reading copies at most 6 books a day, and spell tomes and skill books cannot be copied.

sections.heading: Other fixes
items: A lockpicking attempt cut short by a crash or disconnect no longer stops you picking any other lock until the next restart.
Coin purses and wisp stalks stay picked after a restart.

title: Client 0.3.67: Name Your Character, True Weapon Numbers, Fairer Prayers

sections.heading: Character creation
items: A character that comes out of creation without a name now gets a panel to name it: type the name and choose Take this name. The panel takes typing even when the game's own name box does not.
If a name will not do, the panel says why and stays open for another try. Names follow the same rules as character creation and are unique across the realm.
A name typed into the game's own name box now follows the same rules. If it will not do, you are asked for another before you leave the Realm, and your look is kept.
You leave the Realm once your character is named. Characters already out in the world as "Prisoner" are asked too. On an older client, /name in the chat still works.

sections.heading: Weapons and armor
items: The damage and armor numbers in your inventory now match what the server actually uses: your skill tier, the weapon's material and your Defense are all counted in them.
Improving an item at a grindstone or workbench now really counts in a fight: a weapon gains +1 (Fine) up to +10 (Legendary) damage, a cuirass +2 up to +20 armor and other pieces half that.

The shown damage is a normal blow against a monster; against another player you deal a quarter more. The game's own skill screen now reads 0 for One-Handed, Two-Handed, Archery and the armor skills: they never counted, your tiers in the Skills menu (K) do.

sections.heading: Praying
items: The verses now wait until you press and hold Space (or hold the bar with the mouse), so a slow start or a slow-loading window no longer ruins the prayer, and a held key that briefly drops out picks up again.

sections.heading: Vampires and werewolves
items: Vampirism and lycanthropy now take three game days of your own play to set in, so time logged out no longer counts. A circlet no longer shields a vampire's head from the sun: wear a hood or a helmet.

If your game crashes or your connection drops during a rite, the rounds you already played decide it: behind, the rite is lost, but a disconnect never ends a character for good; even or ahead, the rite is called off and nobody dies.
The Blood Crown no longer stays with a character that was deleted: it lies unclaimed for the next pure-blood.

sections.heading: Main menu
items: Skyrim's own main menu no longer shows behind ours: our title screen is the only one. A main menu replacer you install yourself would show behind it again.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: When your connection drops, the HUD and any open panels now close with it instead of staying on screen.

sections.heading: Getting it
items: The launcher downloads this update the next time you press Play.

sections.heading: Cyrodiil
items: Wisp stalks across Bruma can be harvested (Harvesting improves the yield); a picked stalk grows back after a while.
Ayleid wells restore your magicka and make it flow back faster for five minutes, once a day for each traveller: drink again after midnight.

sections.heading: Character creation
items: Characters made in the last few hours came out named "Prisoner" because the name box in character creation did not take typing. If that happened to you, type /name and your character's name in the chat, for example /name Aela Brightwater. It follows the same rules as character creation, and works once. We are fixing the name box itself.

title: Client 0.3.66: Steadier Around Crowds, and Stuck Cursor Logging

sections.heading: Stability
items: When several enemies come into view at once, your game now takes them over a few at a time instead of all in the same instant. That moment has come just before some crashes, most often on entering a ruin with others.

sections.heading: Menus
items: For the few players whose menu cursor stays stuck in the middle of the screen (character creation included), this update records why, and smooths out mouse input that very fast gaming mice send faster than the game can take. Nothing changes for everyone else. Restart the launcher to get the update.

title: Client 0.3.65: Character Select Works for Everyone

sections.heading: Character select
items: Fixed for the few players whose mouse did nothing at character select: on some setups the game's own menu cursor stayed stuck in the middle of the screen, so every click landed on empty space. When that happens now, our menu follows your mouse itself and your clicks land where you point. Restart the launcher to get the update.

sections.heading: Stability
items: Behind-the-scenes logging to track down a crash when a group enters a ruin together. Nothing changes in play. Restart the launcher to get the update.

title: Client 0.3.63: Shouts You Can See, a Better Trade Request

sections.heading: Shouts
items: Other players now see your shouts, not just your shouting pose: the wave, the breath and the rest play for everyone nearby, and the server still decides what they do to anyone they hit.

sections.heading: Trading
items: A trade request is now a proper card near the top of the screen: who wants to trade, a clear Accept and Decline, and the key that gives you the cursor. Escape hands the cursor back to the game. It no longer sits under the Interact prompt.

sections.heading: Character select
items: More behind-the-scenes logging to track down character select not responding for a few players. Nothing you type is recorded. Restart the launcher to get the update.

sections.heading: Shouts
items: Slow Time is no longer a shout players can learn or use: it slowed the world only on the shouter's own screen, which does not work with other players around. Anyone who has it loses it the next time they log in.

title: Client 0.3.62: Finding the Character Select Issue

sections.heading: Character select
items: If character select doesn't respond to your mouse or keyboard, this update sends us what the menu sees at that moment, on its own, so we can find the cause. Nothing is recorded of what you type. Restart the launcher to get the update.

title: Client 0.3.61: Helping Us Fix Character Select

sections.heading: Character select
items: A few players can see character select but can't click or type anything. This update records what the game sees at that screen so we can find the cause. If it happens to you, press Report a Problem in the launcher right after: it sends us exactly what we need. Restart the launcher to get the update.

sections.heading: Launcher
items: Installing works again without a Nexus sign-in. Since 2.1.31 a player not signed in to Nexus could not install.
Report a Problem works more than once: the button no longer stays greyed out after your first report.
The launcher now tells staff whether the game crashed or was closed, with the exit code and the time, so crashes can be looked into. No logs or files are sent for this.

sections.heading: Character select
items: Character select no longer disappears or loses the mouse when the game's own main menu reports itself late.

sections.heading: Loot
items: Dungeons across Bruma now follow the expeditions' leaner loot: about half the treasure per clear, least on Novice, with big chests usually holding one or two things and urns mostly empty.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: If your mouse did nothing at character select or the main menu, that is fixed. On a fresh install, the Community Shaders mod opened a hidden setup window behind our menu that swallowed every click and key; it is now answered for you. The game also wakes up a mouse that stopped responding and takes the screen back from a window left open in front of it, such as Task Manager. Restart the launcher to get the update.
Stairs your party already opened in a ruin now show as open when you join the expedition later.

sections.heading: Loot
items: Every ruin now gives about half the treasure it did, least on Novice. Big chests usually hold one or two things, urns are mostly empty, the master's chest holds a handful (a raid's about half again as much), and enchanted and Ayleid finds are rarer. The finest Ayleid pieces remain Master-only.

sections.heading: Expeditions
items: Expeditions are now Boss dungeons (for up to 6, one master: Niryastare and Telepe) or Raids (for up to 12: Silorn and Bawn). The Expedition Board shows which is which.
Raid masters are stronger and bring escorts, a raid holds more foes, and its boss chests and masters give more treasure with a better shot at rare Ayleid pieces.
Skill gain is no longer halved for a big group inside a raid ruin. There is no minimum group size, but a raid is built for many: a small party will find it very hard.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: The buttons in Rielle and Anga now lower their retracting stairs, as in Telepe and Silorn.

sections.heading: Scholar
items: Reading a book now draws from 88 new lines of lore: Saint Alessia and Pelinal, the Remans and the Septims, the Wolf Queen, the Dragon War, the Night of Tears, the Tribunal, the Daedric Princes, the fall of Yokuda and more. Novice readers get far more short lines, so the same sentence comes up much less often.

sections.heading: Loot
items: Dungeon loot is leaner: potions turn up far less often (strong ones rarely), and Ayleid treasure now depends on the difficulty. Novice ruins give plain Ayleid gear, and only a Master's boss chest can hold Eminent jewellery or the Ayleid Lich Helmet.
Ruin masters now carry real treasure: loot the master's body for boss-grade coin and gear (Silorn's lich included), and the chest right behind Silorn's lich is now its boss chest.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: A ruin button you have already pressed says so once, instead of filling your chat.

title: Martial Arts, Breaking Things Down, and a New Border

sections.heading: Martial Arts
items: Unarmed is now Martial Arts: fists, quarterstaves and battle staves. Your Unarmed progress carries over.
Every punch that lands drains your opponent's stamina, and a tired fighter hits much weaker, so a boxer who stays close can wear anyone down.
Fists do little against armour; their strength is stamina and the disarm: an unarmed power attack that lands knocks the weapon out of your opponent's hands.
Quarterstaves and battle staves now train and scale with Martial Arts instead of Blunt, and they partly ignore armour.

sections.heading: Breaking things down
items: The breakdown menus now actually open: at a smelter, tanning rack or loom, and at the Scholars' Ledger in the Synod Conclave. Before, nothing showed up.
Items that come enchanted are never offered for breakdown, just like ones you enchant yourself.
You can drag the menu to move it, and it stays where you put it while you break things down.

sections.heading: The world
items: Aleswell's border has moved to where a player showed us it looks right, and a new edge stops you falling into the pit below Fort Caractacus. Outlaw Endre's Cave stays reachable.
Aleswell and Fort Caractacus no longer show twice on the map and compass, and Fort Caractacus is spelled right.
The Book Breakdown Ledger is now the Scholars' Ledger everywhere.
More expedition boards stand in Frostcrag Spire, and all of them now say "Read Expedition Board" instead of "Read Notice Board".
Ruins are dark: carry a torch. You can pick up the torches you find lying around (each one comes back after a while), and big chests in dungeons and expedition ruins often hold one or two.

Expedition ruins now hide Ayleid treasure: bows, swords, daggers, staves, mage robes and Ayleid jewellery turn up in their big chests, and the master's chest always holds a piece, sometimes Eminent jewellery or the Ayleid Lich Helmet.
The buttons in Telepe and Silorn now open their stairs and the treasure-room gate for your whole party, and they stay open until the expedition ends.

sections.heading: Discord
items: Discord skill roles now show only your three highest skills, each once it reaches 25 (Apprentice), instead of every skill you have tried. Your Unarmed role is now called Martial Arts.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Several fixes from a security review of this morning's update, including breaking rings down and sharing coin from a dungeon chest.
Hunting contracts are closed for a short while, and renting out storage chests is paused, while they get a fix.
Long messages in the middle of the screen now wrap instead of running off the edges, and no panel is taller than the screen or cuts its text off.
Your gold now shows on the HUD, updated the moment you are paid or spend it.

sections.heading: For staff
items: The Place tool can now edit, move, tilt and undo what you place, save groups as sets for events, and run warbands from its own tab. Placed NPCs now spawn like every other NPC.
Torches, the Draught of Revival and its recipe are in the admin item menu.

title: The Business Ledger, Scrolls and Shouts, the U Menu and More

sections.heading: The business ledger
items: A business now keeps a real ledger book. When you open your property as a business (/business open <name>), the ledger appears in front of you; set it on a counter with its arrows.

Activate the ledger to run the business from a panel: the week's and the month's takings, the bed rent, a logbook for notes, the record of every rental and change, your staff, and storage chests for rent.
Anyone else who opens it sees the price of a bed, the storage for rent and the hold's tax.
The /business commands still work.

sections.heading: The world
items: The border south of Bruma now lets you walk to Aleswell, Fort Caractacus and the Ayleid well east of them.

sections.heading: The economy
items: The weekly reckoning is on: every claimed property pays its territory's tax, set by the faction's leader or the hold's Jarl or Count, and guards and soldiers are paid their wages from the treasury.
Nobody can pay themselves from a treasury they control, the week's wages are capped at a share of the treasury, and a property's value can only be reassessed once a week.

sections.heading: Shouts
items: Shouts now work against other players, and a draugr's shouts now work on you.
Unrelenting Force: the first word staggers, while the second and third throw the target back, the third hardest.
Disarm makes the target put away the weapons in their hands. They can draw them again straight away, and nobody can be disarmed more than once every 10 seconds.
Dismaying Shout leaves the target terrified and slowed to half speed for 5, 8 or 12 seconds, by the number of words.
Only characters who have been taught shouts can use them, and only the shouts the Dragonborn learns. The breath of dragons stays with the dragons.
The Greybeards will teach the Voice one day, and it won't be easy to learn.

sections.heading: Scrolls
items: Reading a scroll now casts it. Before, the casting played, nothing happened and the scroll came back.
The scroll is used up when you cast it, as it should be.
Every kind of scroll works: fire and frost bolts, summons, armour, cloaks and paralysis.

sections.heading: Your spellbook
items: Spells now live in a spellbook with no limit, and you keep 3 of them prepared. Change which ones are prepared at a magic college (the Synod in Bruma). Type /spells to open it.
If you know more than 3 spells, your first 3 stay prepared and the rest wait in your book.

You can also open your spellbook and change your prepared spells at the Scholars' Ledger in the Synod Conclave: use it and choose "Open your Spell Book". Its other choice, "Break down old books", is for Scholars.

sections.heading: The U menu and fewer commands
items: Press U for a menu of everything you can do, sorted by topic. /help opens it too.
/help is much shorter: it lists only the commands you can use, and tells you where to go for the rest (a bank counter, a notice board, a shrine, K for skills, F3 for factions).
New /status shows your hunger, rest, Death's Chill, jail time, level points and more in one line.
Some commands were merged: /contract, /commission, /party leave, /spells forget and /property mine. The old names still work.

sections.heading: Faction gear
items: A faction's own armor and weapons can now only be made by that faction's smiths and tailors, or by its leader. Anyone else is told who can make it.
In a war, only fighters wearing their faction's uniform count at a standard. Wars are not open yet.

sections.heading: Inns
items: Every bed in an inn can now be rented, not just one or two, whether or not someone owns the inn. Use a free bed to rent it.
If you own an inn, you can keep one of its beds as your own: use it and choose "Make this my bed". Nobody else can rent it or sleep in it, and you can sleep in it for free.
To keep a different bed, choose "Make this my bed" on that one instead, and your old bed goes back up for rent. "This is no longer my bed" puts it back up for rent too.
A bed someone is renting can't be kept until their rent runs out, so nobody is thrown out of a room they paid for.
Your inn's other beds are for your guests: as the owner you sleep only in the bed you keep. Rent prices and the hold's share are unchanged.

sections.heading: Breaking things down
items: You can now break weapons, armour and books down into materials, at the station of the trade that makes them: metal at a smelter (Blacksmith), leather and hide at a tanning rack (Skinner), cloth at a loom (Tailor), and books at the Scholars' Ledger in the Synod Conclave or at a writing desk, such as the ledger in the Restful Watchman (Scholar).

Use the station and choose what to break down. Your tier decides how much comes back: a quarter of the materials as a Novice, up to three quarters as a Master, and always at least one of the main material. A Blacksmith can only melt the metals their tier can work.
A book gives two sheets of paper and a leather strip, and a note or letter gives one sheet.
Only the metal, leather and cloth come back. Gems, soul gems, Daedra hearts and other ingredients in a recipe are lost.
Only plain copies can be broken down. Anything you are wearing or holding, and anything enchanted, improved, renamed or poisoned, is never offered, so you can't lose a good sword by mistake.
If you carry something to break down, the station shows the list first. To use the station as usual, choose its first row and use it again.

sections.heading: Loot
items: Daedra hearts are now extremely rare finds.

sections.heading: Expeditions
items: Expeditions now start from the Expedition Board in the Synod Conclave or the Fighters Guild: use it to pick a ruin and set out with your party. Typing /expedition no longer starts one.
Every expedition ruin now has a boss. When the last one falls, your party has 10 minutes to gather the loot (with a warning at 2 minutes) before anyone still inside is taken home.
Niryastare's arrival is back on its entrance floor, and each ruin's arrival reminds you how to leave: its door, or /expedition leave.
If you can't find the great door, /expedition leave takes your party home from anywhere in the ruin.
Silorn's arrival point has moved to a safer spot.

sections.heading: Hermaeus Mora
items: His blessing now works: while you carry it, a finished reading round counts twice for your Scholar skill, and a skill book can turn up in a dungeon chest you open or a body you loot.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Mining: sitting at a vein's pickaxe marker no longer gives ore. Strike the seam itself.
Werewolves: feeding in beast form now eases your hunger like a meal.
Going down: nobody can finish you in your first 3 seconds, and after that only a weapon or bare hands can. Spells and lingering effects no longer end your down.
Going down: Give up opens after 15 seconds, so a friend has time to reach you.
A Jarl must now be a Nord or an Imperial.
Animals with no hide worth skinning (slaughterfish, mudcrabs, chickens) can be looted again, and a boar now gives two tusks and some leather when skinned.
Some poisons and potions could not be brewed even with the right ingredients. That's fixed.
The emote wheel works again: its emotes and its Cancel button no longer do nothing. The Skills menu had the same fault and is fixed too.

sections.heading: For staff
items: The Place tool (F7 > Place) works again: Enter no longer opens the chat while placing, a readout shows what you are placing, "Placed near me" lists what was placed around you with Go to and Remove, and the catalog can be searched (statics included). What you may place goes by staff tier.

sections.heading: Updating
items: The launcher downloads this update the next time you press Play.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: The field of view setting works now. Set it in Settings and it applies in game straight away, in first and third person and in menus. In 2.1.31 it wrote the value to a file Skyrim doesn't read it from.

sections.heading: Updating
items: The launcher offers the update the next time you open it.

title: Moving Straight Away, Aleswell, and Meals That Take Time

sections.heading: Fixes
items: After you load in, the game now reconnects your keyboard by itself if it isn't receiving your key presses, so you shouldn't have to alt-tab before you can move.

sections.heading: The world
items: The border south of Bruma now takes in Aleswell, Fort Caractacus and the Ayleid well east of them, so you can walk there.

sections.heading: Eating and drinking
items: Eating takes about 5 seconds and drinking about 7, with the time shown on screen. Your hunger goes down when you finish.
You can walk while you eat, at half speed. Sprinting, attacking or drawing a weapon stops the meal, and the rest goes to waste. If your weapon was already out, only an attack stops it.
Eating more during a meal makes it last longer.

sections.heading: Updating
items: The launcher downloads this update the next time you press Play.

sections.heading: Expeditions
items: Four Ayleid ruins far to the south of Cyrodiil are open as expeditions: Niryastare (Kvatch County), Silorn (Skingrad County), Bawn (Bravil County) and Telepe (Leyawiin County).

Set out from Bruma: in the Synod Conclave or the Fighters Guild, type /expeditions to see the ruins and whether they are free, then choose one and your difficulty. Your party in the same hall comes with you.
Each expedition is a one-hour claim like any dungeon, with its own enemies, from Ayleid undead and a lich to bandits, and chests to loot, some of them locked.
Use the ruin's great door to come home to the hall you left from. Your hour running out or logging out brings you back there too.
Joining late? Type /expeditions in the same hall to go and meet your party.

sections.heading: Downloads
items: Mods you already downloaded with Vortex are used as they are. Nothing is downloaded again or copied.

With a free Nexus account, each missing mod opens its Nexus page one at a time: click Slow download and the launcher does the rest, with nothing to move by hand. Sign in to Nexus in the top bar first.
The launcher only borrows Nexus "Mod Manager Download" links while an install is waiting for downloads, then gives them back to Vortex, so Vortex and its collections work normally again.

sections.heading: Also new
items: The server badge shows how many people are online.
Once the game window opens, the launcher steps aside so the game gets your keyboard.
Your microphone is no longer opened when the launcher starts.
A field of view setting in Settings (it works from launcher 2.1.32 on).
Report a Problem no longer sends your chat.

sections.heading: Updating
items: The launcher offers the update the next time you open it.

title: The Great Hunt, Ranks of the Blood, and Getting Back Up

sections.heading: The Great Hunt: werewolf ranks
items: Every werewolf now climbs five ranks by living as one: Fledgling, Prowler, Hunter, Blood-Howler and Elder. Type /hunt to see your rank, your renown and what the next rank brings.
Renown comes from feeding in beast form (an animal 5, a person 10, a player you brought down 60), from each kill in beast form (2) and from each change (2).
In beast form you can now feed on any fresh body, animal or person.

Higher ranks stay in beast form longer (up to 5 minutes at Elder), gain more time from each feed, can change more times each game day and are forced into the change far less often. The beast also hits harder and takes less damage, up to 20% at Elder, against players too.
A player you feed on only counts if you brought them down yourself, outdoors and away from the city, once a day per person, and never your party or your own characters.
When a werewolf howls, everyone in the land hears it echo through the region.
A cure starts you over as a Fledgling.

sections.heading: Ranks of the blood: vampires
items: Vampires climb their own ranks by feeding on people: Fledgling, Vampire, Nightstalker, Mistwalker and Master Vampire. Type /blood to see yours.
Blood comes from a fresh body (5), a living captive (20) or a player you brought down (30), with the same once-a-day rules as the Hunt.
Each rank makes your hits land harder at night (up to 10%), softens the sun's burn (up to 40%) and slows your thirst (up to 40%). By day there is no damage bonus.
The ranks of the blood are gentler than the Hunt's, since vampires are more common. Vampire Lord stays the Blood Crown's alone.

sections.heading: Becoming a werewolf is harder
items: A werewolf's bite now passes on the curse 2% of the time (it was 5%), and surviving Hircine's rite brings it 25% of the time (it was 50%).

sections.heading: Going down and getting back up
items: When you go down, a panel shows how long you have left, who can raise you, and a Give Up button that takes you to the temple.
Players near someone who is down see a countdown over them.
After a revive you are not straight back in the fight: you kneel for 15 seconds while your health climbs back to a quarter, and until you stand nobody can hit you and you cannot hit anyone.

sections.heading: Business ledgers
items: Own an inn or a shop? Stand inside and type /business open <name> to keep its ledger. /business shows your takings and /business collect pays them out.
Set the price of your beds with /business rent <gold>, keep a logbook only you and your staff can read with /business note <text>, and take someone on with /business staff add <name>.
Rent out storage: /business chest <gold a day>, then open the chest. Renters choose 1, 3 or 7 days. A rented chest is theirs alone, with 3 days' grace to empty it afterwards.
A share of every bed and chest rent goes to the hold. Its Jarl, Count or Steward sets that tax, up to 30%, with /tax <percent>.
Takings earned while you are offline are paid when you log in.

sections.heading: Treasuries
items: Every hold's treasury is now kept in the bank instead of a chest. The gold the chests held has moved into the bank.

sections.heading: Crafting and gathering
items: Tundra Cotton now grows in the hills east of Bruma. Pick it to spin thread.
Tailors get a loom in Bruma right after this update, so Tundra Cotton becomes thread and clothes can be made.
The Tailor skill's hint no longer shows a leftover development note.

sections.heading: Magic
items: Summon Skeleton now raises the skeleton that matches your race. Imperials and other races it does not list get a human skeleton instead of one that never appeared, and every summoned skeleton now leaves when its time is up.
Ayleid wells now give the Fortify Magicka half of the Boon of the Ayleids as well as refilling your magicka.

sections.heading: Maps
items: The Realm tab of the faction panel (F3) shows the game's own map icons: Castle Bruma, and the town, settlement and fort markers of Applewatch, Greenwood and Pale Pass.
Aleswell, a town south of Bruma, and Fort Caractacus beside it are now on the world map, and on the Realm map as a town and a fort of their own.

sections.heading: Combat
items: Spells cast from scrolls now count as spell hits, so a paralysis scroll holds the one it hits.
Whether a hit is blocked is now decided from the defender's side, the same for everyone.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Voice chat: a fix for the echo that players on speakers sent back to everyone.
Timber Wolves and summoned Dremora Lords now have the health their level gives them, not a flat 100.
Robbery: only the one who brought you down can rob you, nobody can make a demand in the middle of a fight, and pressing Escape on the robbery panel refuses at once (fight or flee).
The offer to choose a god no longer gets lost when you log in.
A paralysis hold lasts its full time even if someone carries or ties you up and lets go.
In the bank, pressing Enter in the amount box no longer makes a deposit on its own.
Up and Down keep stepping through your chat history after a message of several lines.

sections.heading: Updating
items: Restart the launcher to get client 0.3.53. The new plugin with the Tundra Cotton comes with it.

title: Capitals, the Silver Hand and a Skyrim Pack

sections.heading: Capitals
items: A faction's leader, or a hold's ruler, can now choose the faction's capital from the Realm tab of the faction panel (F3).
A hold picks one of its own territories. Any other faction can pick a territory it holds, or make the spot where the leader stands its seat, such as a guildhall, indoors or out.
Capitals are marked on the map: a crown over a capital territory, and a banner in the faction's colour for a seat.
A capital can move once a week, and not while the faction is at war. Taking a hold's capital, wherever its ruler has put it, takes the hold.

sections.heading: Factions
items: The Companions are an honourable order of warriors again, with no werewolves. Their officers are now Elders of Jorrvaskr.
New: Hircine's Pack of Falkreath, a secret werewolf pack of Skyrim. As with every pack, only werewolves can join, and packs see each other's hunting grounds.
New: The Silver Hand, werewolf hunters who broke away from the Companions.

sections.heading: Other changes
items: The map of the County of Bruma now fills its frame.
The Bruma bank counts as Bruma, so entering it no longer sends you back to Pale Pass.
A player who sleeps in a bed to log out now leaves the world at once, instead of their body standing in the inn for several minutes.
Wisp stalks can be harvested for Wisp Stalk, and the Ayleid wells restore your magicka once per night.
Restart the launcher to get client 0.3.51.

title: The Realm, Peace Treaties and Robbery

sections.heading: The Realm map
items: The faction panel (F3) has a Realm tab: a map of the County of Bruma showing who holds each town, village, fort and the castle, in each faction's own colours. When land changes hands, the borders on the map move with it.
Every hold, clan, guild and order has its colour from the lore, such as yellow for Bruma, red for the Legion and blue for the Stormcloaks. The Companions fly red with a yellow stripe.
Some places are secret. A werewolf pack sees the other packs' hunting grounds, a vampire clan sees the other clans' lairs, and a cult sees only its own shrine. Nobody else sees them.

sections.heading: War (built, not open yet)
items: The rules of war are in place, but war and raids stay closed during the alpha until the holds and factions are set up. The War tab says so.

When war opens, a Jarl, Count, Chieftain or faction leader declares it from the War tab. Both sides need 10 members online, the war costs 10,000 gold from the treasury, and there is a week's notice before three evening battle windows.
To declare, every member of your faction who is online must be gathered at your capital. For Bruma that means Castle Bruma or its grounds.

sections.heading: Peace treaties
items: Leaders who are not at war can swear peace for 1 to 8 weeks from the War tab. One side offers, the other accepts. While the treaty holds, neither side can declare war on the other. This works now.

sections.heading: Treasury
items: Rulers and faction leaders have a Treasury tab. There they set the weekly property tax on homes on their land (0% to 30%) and a weekly wage for each rank. Both start at zero, so nothing is taken until a ruler sets them.

sections.heading: Robbery
items: You can rob someone from the X menu. They get a panel with two choices: Fight or Flee, or Accept Being Robbed. If they give no answer within 20 seconds, it counts as Fight or Flee.
Accepting hands over part of their gold and 3 random items. A key is taken only very rarely. Keep your gold in the bank.

sections.heading: Other changes
items: Gold now has weight: 0.02 a coin, so 1,000 gold weighs 20.
Your field of view is restored after the character creator, instead of staying zoomed in.
Restart the launcher to get client 0.3.50.

sections.heading: The bank
items: Bruma has a bank. Keep your gold there, safe from thieves, looters and raids.
Your account is the same at every bank in the land: gold you put in at one town comes out at another.
Use the bank's counter to open it. Deposit, withdraw, or move everything at once, and see your recent entries.
Jarls, Counts, Chieftains and faction leaders see their treasury in the bank too. They can pay gold in, but no one can take it out; the realm spends it.
No panel yet? Restart the launcher to get client 0.3.49. Until then, /bank at the counter works in chat.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: The flat billboard trees that stood next to the real trees all over Bruma are gone.

sections.heading: What is coming
items: Surviving as a werewolf will be hard. Every new werewolf starts as a weak Fledgling and climbs the ranks by living as one: transforming, hunting and feeding.
Werewolf ranks grow with every creature you feed on. Players are worth far more than animals, but you can rank up on animals alone if you'd rather not hunt people. It just takes longer.
Higher ranks bring more armor, health and stamina in beast form, a longer transformation, new howls, and more control over the change. The highest ranks can change and change back at will.
New howls unlocked by rank: Howl of Rage (speed and regeneration), Howl of the Hunt (track your prey), and at Alpha, Howl of the Pack, which gives your packmates the rage.
Every howl is heard across the land: "A howl echoes through <region>". Hunters will know where to look, so howl with care.

Neglect the beast and it takes you: a werewolf who goes too long without changing and feeding may turn at night without warning. A feral werewolf howls on its own and must feed before it can change back.
Packs will claim territories and hunt there for more rank. Rival packs can declare a territory war and fight for the land over a week.
Werewolves of different ranks will look different, so a seasoned hunter can tell a Fledgling from an Alpha.
Silver ends a werewolf for good. A werewolf in beast form is fair game, and a hunter who goes looking for one takes the same risk.

sections.heading: Already in the game
items: Feeding in beast form keeps the change going longer, hunger and the full moon can force a change, silver hurts, and each pack is led by a pale-coated Alpha who can be challenged.

sections.heading: Where this stands
items: Stage 1, the werewolf ranks, is in the game: see "The Great Hunt, Ranks of the Blood, and Getting Back Up". The rest arrives in stages, and details will change as we build and test it. Designed by swag and the DragonBreak team.

sections.heading: Chat
items: Press Up in the chat box to bring back what you sent before, and Down to go forward again. It remembers your last 20 lines. Restart the launcher to get client 0.3.48.

sections.heading: Help
items: /help is organised by topic, one line each: chat and people, your character, faith, work and the world, rule and property, groups and dungeons, and trouble.
/help <topic> lists that topic with what each command does, for example /help character. /help <command> explains one command, for example /help level.
Staff: /help admin lists the staff commands by topic in the admin tab.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: The server crashes tonight are fixed. When a creature despawned, a late message about it could read memory that had already been freed and take the whole server down.
Scrolls work properly: casting one uses it up and trains Arcane Arts or Priest by its school. The server used to refuse every scroll cast, so scrolls never counted and were never used up.
Sentinel armor can be forged. The server did not recognise those recipes at the forge, cancelled the craft and handed the materials back.
Parties survive a server restart or crash, so friendly fire stays reduced inside your party afterwards.
The party and companion panels clear when the party breaks up or the companion is gone.
A trade request now says "Press X to answer": X gives the request your cursor and Escape hands it back. You no longer need Enter to reach the buttons.
Guard, jail and spell menus that lead to a second menu keep your cursor.
Creatures and NPCs are handled more reliably: when someone leaves or a creature is removed, the one controlling it hands it over cleanly, and a respawn shows for everyone nearby.

sections.heading: New
items: Pickpocketing: sneak up on someone and press X, then choose Pickpocket. Your Lockpicking skill sets the odds, and it is easier from behind and harder against a drawn weapon. You take a little coin or one thing from their pockets, never what they are wearing and never a key. If you are caught, they know at once; if not, they notice what is missing a minute later.

Combat is more about skill: a blocked blow can still chip through and costs the blocker stamina, heavy blows can break a guard, a shield bash deals a little damage and staggers, and power attacks stagger. Veteran defenders resist being bashed off their feet.
Player-on-player damage is up 25%, better weapon materials hit harder, and Destruction spells grow stronger with your Arcane Arts tier.
Surviving Hircine's Great Hunt now gives you Sanies Lupinus instead of turning you on the spot; the fever does the turning once it runs its course.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: The level-up panel no longer disappears for good. Taking beast form used to close it in a way that stopped it ever opening again, so unspent points were stranded. It reopens properly now.
If the panel still will not show, you can spend a point straight from chat: /level health, /level magicka or /level stamina. Plain /level tells you how many you have left.
Choosing a point in the panel no longer closes it when the choice does not take, which used to cost you both the panel and the point.
Players standing near you now see you turn into a beast, and see you return to mortal form afterwards.

Logging in with unspent level points no longer leaves you unable to move. The panel used to take the keyboard; it now opens without stealing it and tells you in chat how to spend. A level gained mid-fight no longer grabs the keys either.
Renting an inn bed no longer loses your cursor. The second prompt used to appear with the mouse turning the camera instead of clicking.
The text after you go down or wake with the chill of the grave is much shorter on screen. The full explanation is in chat, where you can read it back after the banner clears.

sections.heading: Magic
items: New mages can now start at the Synod Conclave in Bruma: read a Novice spell tome there and you take up its school's skill (Arcane Arts for Destruction, Conjuration and Illusion; Priest for Restoration and Alteration) and learn the spell. It uses one skill point, like starting a trade at its bench.

Books you read through can now turn up a scroll tucked between the pages. The better your Scholar skill, the more often it happens and the stronger the scroll can be (up to six a day). Casting scrolls is a way to practise magic before you own a spell.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Tanning racks, chopping blocks, ore veins and other seats no longer stay taken after you walk through a door while using them, and using one again after a failed sit now works.
You can now talk with your push-to-talk key while the trade window or another game window is open.

sections.heading: In this client update (restart the launcher)
items: Client 0.3.42 carries the seat and push-to-talk fixes. Restart the launcher before you log in.

sections.heading: Creatures and enemies
items: Fixed creatures that played their walking animation without going anywhere and only fought what stood right in front of them. The server was wrongly telling your game that another player controlled creatures your game was actually running, so it held them in place. This bug is old; it became much more visible with this evening's update.
When a creature despawns and a new one spawns in the same moment, your game now always builds a fresh copy of the new one.

sections.heading: Server
items: Fixed a short freeze of the whole server that could happen while it saved its live status file.

sections.heading: In this client update (restart the launcher)
items: Client 0.3.41 carries the creature fix above. The launcher will not let 0.3.40 connect, so restart it before you log in.

sections.heading: Creatures and enemies
items: The server now decides whose game runs each creature: the nearest player who has it in view. Before, the first player to ask kept it, even after walking away, so creatures froze, floated or stopped fighting back for everyone else.
Your game now reports where a creature's body really is, not just where the game thinks it stands. This is aimed at creatures that float above the ground or sink into it.
Other players' view of a creature is steadier: less sliding past where it stopped and less snapping back.

sections.heading: Reporting problems
items: New command: /bug <what went wrong>. It saves your report together with where you stand and every creature around you, so the team can see exactly what you saw. One report a minute.

sections.heading: Behind the scenes
items: The server now checks every item that is dropped, stored or taken.
Staff get a live monitor of server, player and creature problems while people play.

sections.heading: In this client update (restart the launcher)
items: Client 0.3.40 carries the body-position and creature-view changes above. Restart the launcher to get it.

sections.heading: Creatures and enemies
items: Creatures no longer stay frozen after the player running them walks away: the server hands them to someone nearby within seconds, so they move and fight back again.
Creatures that sink into the ground are lifted back onto it by the server.
Creatures no longer snap back and forth across the map: the server refuses impossible jumps and puts them back where they belong.
Goblins and other Beyond Skyrim enemies carry their weapons again.

sections.heading: In this client update (restart the launcher)
items: Locked and loot chests in dungeons glow again.
When an archer shoots, other players now see the arrow fly at the target.
Switching characters no longer hides your chat box.
Staff: the Place tab shows its preview and places again.

sections.heading: Skills
items: Taking up a skill you have earned now grants its first abilities straight away.

sections.heading: Support
items: You can now open a support ticket without leaving the game: /ticket <kind> <what happened>. Type /ticket on its own to see the kinds: player kill request, bug, map, moderation help, report a player.
It opens a private channel on Discord that only you and staff can read, the same as the #create-a-ticket panel. Staff answer you there.
Where you are standing and who is nearby are attached for you, which helps staff with reports and kill requests.

sections.heading: Proximity voice
items: Restart the launcher to update. The server asks for 0.3.38 from now on.
Voices now come from where the speaker stands: left, right, in front or behind.
Voices fade more naturally with distance and die away at the edge of hearing instead of cutting off.
A whisper only carries to someone in front of you.
A small list above the voice box shows who is talking.

sections.heading: Lockpicking
items: Jail cell doors and locked dungeon chests are now picked the Oblivion way: one tumbler for each lock level, from one on a Novice lock to five on a Master lock.
Push a tumbler up and set it while it hangs at the top. Set it too early or too late and your pick may snap.
Higher Lockpicking tiers keep tumblers hanging longer and snap fewer picks. Harder locks give you less time.
You need client 0.3.37: restart the launcher.

sections.heading: New in this client
items: Restart the launcher to update. The server asks for 0.3.37 from now on.
The god picker now lists the older faiths (the Hist, the Ancestors, the Yokudan gods, Riddle'Thar, Trinimac and the cults) in their own group.
Staff get a Place tab in the admin menu, to put NPCs and objects into the world for events.
Voice chat is unchanged in this update.

sections.heading: Armour takes time to change in a fight
items: Putting on or taking off armour or clothing within 20 seconds of a blow, dealt or taken, now takes time: 5 seconds for each heavy piece, 3 for each light piece, 2 for clothing and jewellery, up to 30 seconds.
Until the straps are done you move slowly and your blows do not land. Changing again before you are done adds to the time.
Outside a fight nothing changes: dress and undress as you like. Weapons, spells and shields are always free to swap.

sections.heading: Ledgers
items: Everyone you have spoken with in person is written into your ledger. Read it with /ledger at any notice board, inside a house you own or rent, or where a court or guild keeps one.

Contacts sort themselves under the factions you share and under Family (by a shared family name, gro- and gra- alike), then your own groups and acquaintances. File someone with /ledger group <name> Friends, or any group you like.
Keep a private note beside anyone with /ledger note <name> <text>, and send them a letter by pigeon from the ledger with /ledger letter <name> <text>.
/ledger forget <name> strikes someone out. You will know them again only after meeting in person.

sections.heading: Property
items: A hold's Jarl, Steward or other property official can now rent out an empty house at its door, for a deposit and a weekly rent (/property list).

At the door, /property shows the terms and /property interest puts your name down. If the officials offer it to you, come back and say /property accept: you pay the deposit and the first week, and the house and its keys are yours to live in.

Pay rent at the door with /property pay. Rent that falls due is announced; the officials may send a reminder, give a week's grace, or evict, in which case the hold keeps the deposit. Leave in good standing with /property leave and the deposit comes back.
Officials see what they manage with /properties.

sections.heading: Skills
items: One-Handed and Two-Handed are gone. In their place, as in the older Elder Scrolls: Blade (swords, daggers and greatswords, one hand or two) and Blunt (maces, war axes, warhammers and battleaxes).

Your progress moves over the next time you log in, and nothing is lost. It goes to whichever of the two you actually fought with; if you had both skills, the higher one goes to the side you favoured and the other to the other side.
Tier bonuses are unchanged: +35%, +65% and +100% damage at Journeyman, Expert and Master.

sections.heading: Also new today
items: Commissions: post work at a notice board with /commission post, and the reward is held by the board until the work is done. If you disagree over whether it was done, the town's officials settle it.
Offerings: /offer gold at your god's shrine before you pray. Half keeps the town's temple, and your next prayer is likelier to be answered.

sections.heading: Death
items: Waking at the temple now leaves the chill of the grave on you for 20 minutes of play: stamina and magicka stay low and come back slowly, and every heal, potions included, works at half strength.
Being raised in the field by a Priest or a Draught of Revival leaves no chill.
A Priest of the second tier or higher can lift it with a healing spell, or with Grand Healing for everyone close by. Type /chill to see how long is left.

sections.heading: Faith
items: Seven new faiths can be followed by anyone: the Hist, the Ancestors, the Yokudan Gods, the Riddle'Thar, Trinimac, the Dragon Cult and the Worm Cult. None of them needs a shrine: kneel anywhere and type /pray.

Their blessings come more rarely and last half as long as a shrine god's. Each draws on its people's own gift: Histskin, Ancestor's Wrath, Adrenaline Rush, Night Eye, the Lord's protection, the dragons' Voice, or a necromancer's magicka.
The Dragon Cult and the Worm Cult are outlawed in the Empire.

sections.heading: Letters
items: Type /sign unsigned before sending a pigeon and your next letter goes unsigned.
A Scholar of the third tier or higher can sign a letter in someone else's name with /sign <name>. A forger below Master sometimes leaves a hand that does not quite match.

sections.heading: Launcher
items: Report a Problem sends your recent game, SkyrimPlatform and SKSE logs straight to staff, with a report id you can quote on Discord.
Updates leave unchanged client files alone and retry a busy file instead of failing.
The Creation Club archives the server uses are kept in place instead of being moved aside, and any missing ones are filled in for you.
The launcher offers the update itself: accept it once and it installs in place, keeping your settings and login.

sections.heading: Combat
items: Weapon skills hit much harder: +35% damage at Journeyman, +65% at Expert and +100% at Master (was +10/20/30%). A master with a great weapon now brings down an unarmored fighter in about four blows.
Unarmed now gets its tier bonus too. Fists never did before.
Defense makes the armor you wear count for more: +25% at Apprentice, up to +250% at Master. Heavy armor worn with a high Defense skill is now what keeps you standing.

sections.heading: Law and property
items: A bound prisoner is uncuffed when the cell door locks behind them.
Renaming a property no longer breaks keys already cut for it, and it can no longer hand them to another property of the same name.

sections.heading: The Synod tome shop
items: The Synod sells only the spell tomes known in Cyrodiil. Tomes from Skyrim and Solstheim will be sold in their own lands.

sections.heading: Bruma
items: The Fighters Guild hall, its basement and Icewind Traders have been rebuilt, with more changes around the city streets. Your launcher downloads the updated file the next time you press Play.

sections.heading: Trade and shops
items: The trade window now shows where the trade stands: each side's Accept is shown, there is one Accept button and a gold field, and you are warned when a change resets the other side's Accept.
The Synod's tome shop has its own panel: school tabs, books grouped by rank, a search bar, a countdown to your next weekly purchase, and a confirmation before you buy.

sections.heading: Party and characters
items: The party panel has a Leave button, with a confirmation click.
Quitting to the main menu now takes you back to character select.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Drinking or eating no longer locks a drawn weapon in place.
Console commands such as god mode, no-clip and changing your stats are for staff only, and every use is logged.

sections.heading: Character creation
items: Choosing a god is now the last step of making a new character. When you finish shaping your character, the god menu opens before you leave the Realm.
Pick one then, or press Not yet to decide later: type /deity whenever you are ready. Your first choice is always free, and changing gods later still takes a week.

sections.heading: Combat
items: Bows and crossbows now add your arrows' damage to every hit, as in the base game. A hunting bow with iron arrows hits about twice as hard as before, and better arrows add more.
A player finished off while down now wakes at the temple at full health.

sections.heading: Dungeons and enemies
items: Every enemy in a dungeon is now there for everyone in it, wherever you stand. They no longer vanish when you leave a room, and they keep hunting you through the halls.
Enemies now appear where they belong instead of bunching up around one player. This also fixes hits that failed to land on them, and wildlife hopping or bouncing in place.
Updating the server no longer ends a dungeon run in progress.

sections.heading: Magic and vitals
items: Healing Hands now heals the player you aim it at instead of yourself.
Magicka no longer fills up and then drops back while it regenerates, and your bars stay in step with the server.

sections.heading: Party and trade
items: Your party's health shows again after someone crashes or relogs.
The trade window has a search bar that filters your inventory and both offers.

sections.heading: Mining
items: Sea Salt Deposits can now be mined. Work one like an ore seam to scrape out Salt Piles, and now and then some Frost, Fire or Void Salts with them. Any Miner can work them.
Sea Salt Deposits now crop up in the hills around Bruma: five of the bare veins between the watchtowers and the southern slopes have turned to salt.

The Geode Veins of Whistling Mine (and of Blackreach) can now be cracked open by a Miner of the second tier. Each holds one empty soul gem: usually a Petty or Lesser one, sometimes a Common or Greater, and rarely a Grand. Never a Black one.
Every other geode now gives the gem it is named for: Amethyst and Topaz from the second Miner tier, Ruby and Sapphire from the third, Emerald from the fourth, Diamond at the fifth.

sections.heading: A potion that raises the fallen
items: Alchemists of the fourth tier can now brew the Draught of Revival. Carry one to a fallen ally and press E on them to pour it in: they get up where they lay with a quarter of their health. Drinking it while facing them works too.
